items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Exported APIs, the ring buffer and the precedence rules are well documented. However, the business logic uses single-letter locals (`s := &b.durable`, `j, err := d.durability.lookupJob(...)`, `t.mu.jobs[...]`), which hits the cap.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is a cleanly separated tracker with short functions. Coupling leaks out of it, though: `reflect.ValueOf(fn).Pointer()` sentinel checks detect a configured callback, `batch.durable.db = d` lets `Batch.SyncWait` call back into DB, and applyInternal has duplicated batchDurable branches.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It is concurrency-safe, retention and subscription limits are bounded by named constants, and close/ctx precedence is handled. But `info.SyncDuration = max(info.SyncDuration, 1)` makes up a value instead of measuring it, and SyncDuration can include apply time.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API changes are additive. But every sync commit takes the tracker mutex and allocates in broadcastLocked (`t.mu.changed = make(chan struct{})`) even when BatchDurable is unset, and `syncStart`/`applyStart` NowMono calls are added to every commit, sync or not.
